stem: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: LTE Release-8 can support downlink data rates on the order of 1 Gbps.

Peak rate is defined as the maximum throughput that can be achieved per user, assuming whole bandwidth is allocated to a single user with the highest possible modulation/coding order, and when the maximum possible number of antennas are used at the transmitter/receiver.
Peak rates, while an important indicator, may not be a key differentiator for the success of a particular wireless technology, since they are not typically achieved.

stem: An ideal 20 MHz AWGN link has an SNR of 10 dB. Approximately what is its Shannon capacity?
options: 20 Mbps
46 Mbps
69 Mbps
200 Mbps
explanation: 10 dB is a linear SNR of 10. C = 20 million × log2(1+10) ≈ 69.2 Mbps.
source: New item derived from lecture/application concepts

stem: A link delivers 60 Mbps of net user data over a 20 MHz occupied channel. What is its net spectral efficiency?
options: 0.33 bps/Hz
3 bps/Hz
20 bps/Hz
80 bps/Hz
explanation: Net spectral efficiency is delivered rate divided by occupied bandwidth: 60/20 = 3 bps/Hz.

stem: When receiver noise power spectral density and received signal power stay fixed, what happens if an AWGN channel bandwidth is doubled?
options: Noise power doubles and SNR falls by about 3 dB
Noise power stays fixed and SNR stays fixed
Noise power halves and SNR rises by 3 dB
SNR doubles and capacity exactly doubles
explanation: Noise power scales as N0 B. Doubling B doubles integrated noise and lowers SNR by 3.01 dB when signal power is fixed.
